workflows.title: Document Production (report module pattern)
workflows.body:
1. **OUTLINE** — Structure from the brief; confirm sections before writing.
2. **DRAFT** — Write section by section; each section cites its sources.
3. **SELF-QA** — Read the draft as a hostile reviewer: check every number,
   every claim, every formatting rule. Fix-list, not praise.
4. **FORMAT** — Apply the house style (fonts, layout, language rules).
5. **DELIVER** — Final file + a one-paragraph summary of what changed vs.
   the brief.

techniques.title: Translate-and-Re-Lip-Sync (localization as re-render)
techniques.what_it_does: The translation pipeline transcribes the source video, translates the script, synthesizes the speaker's cloned voice in the target language, and then re-renders the avatar's mouth movements to match the new language's phonemes — frame by frame. It is not dubbing; it is a new render.
techniques.why_it_works: Different languages have different phoneme inventories. Only re-rendering against the target audio produces believable sync; testers describe this as the platform's most striking capability.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Treat every localization as a fresh render through T-02's pipeline with translated text as input. Store the source script + language map so a change to the source can re-trigger all localized renders automatically.

techniques.title: Declarative Scene API (video_inputs manifest)
techniques.what_it_does: Videos are created through a declarative JSON manifest: an array of scenes, each specifying character (avatar id + style), voice (text + voice id, or audio asset), background (color, image, or video with playback style), and output dimensions. Generation is asynchronous: submit → poll status → retrieve finished file.
techniques.why_it_works: A video becomes data. Scenes are composable, version-controlled, and machine-generatable; multi-scene videos (1–50 scenes) assemble from the same schema as single scenes.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Adopt a declarative scene manifest as the contract between the report module (which authors scripts) and the avatar host (which renders). Keep generation async with a status poller so long renders never block the scheduler.

prompt_patterns.title: One Concept Per Scene
prompt_patterns.use_when: scripting any video longer than ~30 seconds.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Split the script into scenes; each scene carries exactly one concept, one avatar framing, one background. The scene manifest lists them in order (video_inputs[0..n]).
prompt_patterns.template: > Scene <n>: <one concept> | framing=<head/torso/full> | > background=<ref> | script=<the lines for this scene only>. > If a scene carries two ideas, split it.
prompt_patterns.raw:
- **Use when:** scripting any video longer than ~30 seconds.
- **Pattern:** Split the script into scenes; each scene carries exactly one
  concept, one avatar framing, one background. The scene manifest lists them
  in order (video_inputs[0..n]).
- **Template:**
  > Scene <n>: <one concept> | framing=<head/torso/full> |
  > background=<ref> | script=<the lines for this scene only>.
  > If a scene carries two ideas, split it.

prompt_patterns.title: Plain-Language Script Rule
prompt_patterns.pattern: Short, simple sentences. Spell out acronyms and abbreviations phonetically. Avoid jargon the voice may mispronounce. One breath per sentence.
prompt_patterns.template: > Rewrite each line so a non-expert can read it aloud cold. > Acronyms: write them as they sound (<e.g.> "A-P-I" → "ay pee eye"). > No sentence longer than one spoken breath.
prompt_patterns.raw:
- **Use when:** writing the spoken lines.
- **Pattern:** Short, simple sentences. Spell out acronyms and abbreviations
  phonetically. Avoid jargon the voice may mispronounce. One breath per
  sentence.
- **Template:**
  > Rewrite each line so a non-expert can read it aloud cold.
  > Acronyms: write them as they sound (<e.g.> "A-P-I" → "ay pee eye").
  > No sentence longer than one spoken breath.

prompt_patterns.title: Pronunciation Lexicon Pre-Flight
prompt_patterns.use_when: the script contains brand names, product names, or technical terms.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Before rendering, extract every risky term, write its phonetic spelling, and test it in a draft render. Fix the lexicon, not the take.
prompt_patterns.template: > Terms to verify: <term> → <phonetic spelling>. > Render a 10-second draft with all terms. Listen once; correct the > spelling, not the avatar. Lock the lexicon before the final render.
prompt_patterns.raw:

  terms.
- **Pattern:** Before rendering, extract every risky term, write its

prompt_patterns.title: Beat Timing (hook, pace, CTA)
prompt_patterns.pattern: Hook in the first 3 seconds. Pause between sentences so the delivery breathes. Aim 60–90 seconds for explainers. End with one clear call to action — the last scene exists only for the CTA.
prompt_patterns.template: > Scene 1 (0–3s): the hook — one sentence, the payoff stated up front. > Middle scenes: one concept each, pause <0.5s> between sentences. > Final scene: one clear action for the viewer. Nothing after it.
prompt_patterns.raw:
- **Use when:** structuring any script.
- **Pattern:** Hook in the first 3 seconds. Pause between sentences so the
  delivery breathes. Aim 60–90 seconds for explainers. End with one clear

- **Template:**

  > Middle scenes: one concept each, pause <0.5s> between sentences.
  > Final scene: one clear action for the viewer. Nothing after it.

prompt_patterns.title: Two-Tier Render (draft vs final)
prompt_patterns.pattern: Run every video first at draft quality for internal review; reserve the highest-quality render for the client-facing or published version. Never burn premium render budget on a draft.
prompt_patterns.template: > Round 1: draft tier — check script, sync, framing. > Round 2 (only after Round 1 passes QC): final tier — the version that > ships. Draft failures never reach the final tier.

- **Pattern:** Run every video first at draft quality for internal review;

workflows.title: Localization Pipeline (one video → many languages)
workflows.body:
Owner: avatar host (+ report for translation).

1. **TRANSCRIBE & LOCK** — Transcribe the source video; lock the source
   script. Exit: source script + language map. *Guard:* multi-speaker or
   occluded footage is rejected here (P-07 anti-pattern).
2. **TRANSLATE** — Translate per target language; a human or reviewer pass
   on the transcript before translation for high-stakes content. Exit:
   script_L for each language. *Guard:* unreviewed machine translation is
   flagged draft-only.
3. **VOICE** — Synthesize script_L with the same speaker identity (T-05/
   T-06). Exit: audio_L per language. *Guard:* product-capability only —
   the 369 publish path refuses AI voice at this step.
4. **RE-RENDER SYNC** — Fresh render per language with lip-sync regenerated
   against the new phonemes (T-02, T-06). Exit: video_L per language.
   *Guard:* overlaying audio_L on the source face is rejected by the gate.
5. **QC PER LANGUAGE** — P-09 per language, plus a native-speaker spot check
   on pacing for flagship languages. Exit: per-language PASS/FAIL.
6. **BUNDLE** — Publish the language set with shared manifest. Exit: all
   languages registered; a source-script change re-triggers the pipeline.

techniques.title: Slide-Scene Video Composition (the slide is the atomic unit)
techniques.what_it_does: The editor is built on slides, not timelines. Each slide carries one script segment, one layout, and one set of timing rules; the video is the ordered composition of its slides. PowerPoint decks import directly into this structure.
techniques.why_it_works: Business content already lives in slides. Making the slide the atomic unit removes a translation step — the source document IS the video blueprint. Independent reviewers consistently cite the slide-first editor as Synthesia's core strength for training content.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The report module's video authoring path should treat slides as first-class objects: each slide = {script, layout, assets, duration}. Any external document (PDF, PPTX, doc) imports into a slide manifest first, and generation always runs from the manifest — never from raw free text.

techniques.title: 1-Click Translation as Re-render (localization, not dubbing)
techniques.what_it_does: The translation workflow takes the master script, translates it (dozens of languages), and generates a new video in the target language. Glossary controls keep names, terms and pronunciation consistent across every language. It is a re-render, not an audio overlay — the avatar's mouth is produced against the new language's audio.

Store the master script + glossary + language map so a change to the master can re-trigger all localized renders automatically. Never let the glossary live in someone's head — it is a versioned data artifact.

techniques.title: AI Dubbing Pipeline (finished video in, localized video out)
techniques.what_it_does: Unlike the script path, dubbing accepts a *finished* video: upload an MP4/MOV/WebM file (up to 4K) or paste a video link. The pipeline transcribes it, translates it, synthesizes the speaker's voice in the target language, and re-syncs the lips — with a line-by-line editor for correcting translated lines before final delivery.
techniques.why_it_works: It decouples input from format. Any existing asset — not just script-authored ones — becomes localizable. The correction editor is the key trust point: machine translation is draft-quality, human review is the gate. - **GENESIS implementation (product capability only; voice synthesis included):** Build a re-lip-sync path that accepts rendered video as input: transcribe → translate (glossary-applied) → voice render → lip re-sync → human correction queue → final. The correction queue is mandatory, not optional: no dubbed video exits without a native-speaker or glossary-verified sign-off on hooks and terminology.

techniques.title: AI Video Assistant (document → structured draft)
techniques.what_it_does: An assistant layer turns raw input — a document, a URL, a slide deck, or a plain-text description — into a structured first draft: outline, scenes, and suggested visuals, with brand styling pre-applied. The user then refines through chat (tone, messaging, structure) without starting over. It ships as an always-available drafting mode, not a separate product.
techniques.why_it_works: The hardest part of video production is the blank page. The assistant collapses "idea → structured manifest" into minutes, and chat refinement preserves continuity instead of regenerating from scratch. Independent reviewers note the caveat honestly: the assistant improves *delivery*, not content strategy — a weak source deck stays weak.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The report module should expose a draft mode: source document in → outline + scene manifest + visual suggestions out, all in the same declarative schema as T-08. Refinement happens as amendments to the manifest (same amend() mechanics as our scheduler), never as a blind regenerate.

techniques.title: Living-Document Version Control (edit once, propagate everywhere)
techniques.what_it_does: Videos are not frozen files — they are living documents. Edit the master and every published copy updates automatically: shared links, website embeds, and LMS-delivered SCORM packages. Version history and analytics (views, completion, per-language comparison) attach to the document, not to a file.
techniques.why_it_works: It eliminates the version-drift problem that makes video programs expensive: a correction no longer means tracking down and replacing every copy in circulation. This is the defining "video *program*" feature versus a "make a video" tool.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Every GENESIS-produced video artifact should carry a master-id; derived copies (embeds, translations, LMS packages) are renders of the master, not independent files. A master edit triggers re-render of dependents with a change log. This is the single most program-grade pattern in the pack — adopt it as a platform-wide artifact convention, not just for avatar video.

techniques.title: Interactive Video Layer (from broadcast to conversation)
techniques.what_it_does: Videos can carry clickable CTAs, branching paths, and quizzes — the viewer chooses what happens next. A newer product line adds roleplay sessions (practice real conversations with an avatar: sales calls, feedback, complaints — scored), and a real-time interactive avatar API that embeds lip-synced conversational avatars in third-party products.
techniques.why_it_works: It converts one-way broadcast into a loop: the video measures the viewer (quiz scores, branch choices, roleplay ratings), and the measurements feed back into the training program. techniques.genesis_implementation: Design the avatar host's output schema to support interaction nodes (CTA / branch / quiz) as first-class scene types, and design the real-time path as a pluggable rendering layer behind a conversation interface (transcribe → reason → synthesize → render). Roleplay scoring is a product-capability pattern the training side of GENESIS can reuse: scenario card + rubric + scored transcript.

techniques.title: Provenance and Compliance Stack (machine-readable proof)
techniques.what_it_does: The platform ships C2PA content credentials and AI labels with every video (machine-readable proof of origin that travels with the file), holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 42001 (first AI video company to achieve it) and GDPR compliance, maintains a dedicated Trust & Safety team, participates in the Content Authenticity Initiative, and honors data-deletion requests from depicted persons.
techniques.why_it_works: Compliance is the enterprise buying criterion. C2PA credentials make provenance verifiable by machines, not just promised in marketing. ISO 42001 specifically addresses AI management systems — the standard that matters when a tool generates synthetic media of employees.
techniques.genesis_implementation: Every artifact the GENESIS build pipeline produces should carry provenance metadata (source, engine version, consent reference, timestamp) in a machine-readable envelope — our own C2PA-style practice. This directly serves our verification-first laws (VERIFY-BEFORE-REPORT): an artifact without provenance is not shippable.

workflows.title: Script-to-Video Lifecycle (the master workflow)
workflows.body:
The canonical production path. Every avatar video job follows it.

1. **INTAKE** — Receive the brief: audience, outcome, source script or
   document. Entry: brief names the audience and the one thing the viewer
   must know after. Exit: scope written down, or one clarifying question.
2. **CAST** — Select avatar + voice persona (P-03), aspect ratio, brand
   profile. Entry: brief approved. Exit: test-render probe of 1–2 slides
   approved (P-08); otherwise re-cast.
3. **BUILD** — Author the scene manifest: slides with per-slide beats
   (P-01), glossary declared (P-04), layout locked.
   Exit: manifest passes schema validation (variables named, fallbacks set).
4. **PREVIEW** — Watermarked probe render of the full manifest.
   Exit: pacing check (≥3s per on-screen text), layout on target aspect
   ratio, hard-word pronunciation passes; fix-list otherwise.
5. **MODERATE** — Script policy gate (T-12): business-appropriate content
   only; flagged items to a human review queue.
   Exit: PASS, or rejected with the specific policy reason.
6. **RENDER** — Final generation, async with status poll (T-08).
   Exit: file produced, hash recorded, provenance envelope attached (T-13).
7. **PUBLISH** — Deliver as link/embed/package with version id; master
   registered for living-document updates (T-09).
   Exit: published copy is a *derived render* of the registered master.

**Guarded failure modes:** lip-sync glitch on fast dialogue → re-render the
affected scene only (never the whole video blind); moderation rejection →
the job stops with the reason, never proceeds silently; deleted identity
referenced → substitute must be re-cast, dependents flagged for re-render.

workflows.title: Document-to-Video Conversion (source in, teaching out)
workflows.body:
For source material that starts as a PDF, deck, or URL.

1. **INGEST** — Pull the source; extract text, structure, and assets.
   Entry: source file/URL accessible. Exit: raw extract + asset list, or
   "source unreadable" reported with evidence.
2. **OUTLINE** — Editorial pass (P-02): ≤7 teaching beats, audience-first.
   Exit: outline approved by the requester. *Failure guard:* a weak source
   deck is flagged here, not carried into production — the assistant
   improves delivery, not content strategy.
3. **SCENES** — Expand each beat into a slide manifest (P-01), visuals
   attached, glossary declared (P-04).
   Exit: manifest validated; every claim in the source marked
   verified/unverified.
4. **REFINE** — Chat-style amendment of the manifest (tone, structure,
   messaging) — amendments, never blind regenerates.
   Exit: requester signs off on the manifest.
5. **RENDER → PUBLISH** — Hand off to W-01 stages 5–7 (moderate, render,
   publish with version id).

**Guarded failure modes:** unverified claims from the source are carried
as on-screen "source unverified" flags, never narrated as facts; exceeding
7 beats → split into a series, not a longer video.

workflows.title: Global Localization Run (one master, every market)
workflows.body:
1. **LOCK MASTER** — The source-language video is published and version-
   pinned (T-09). Entry: master render passed W-01. Exit: master id + hash.
2. **GLOSSARY** — Declare/refresh the term glossary (P-04): names,
   products, pronunciation notes, per-language keep-vs-translate rules.
   Exit: glossary versioned; no video with undeclared names proceeds.
3. **TRANSLATE** — Script translated per target language; hooks and CTAs
   flagged for native-speaker review (P-07).
   Exit: translated scripts + review sign-offs for hooks/CTAs.
4. **RE-RENDER** — Fresh render per language against the translated audio
   (T-05); dubbed-from-finished-video assets go through the dub pipeline
   with the line-by-line correction editor (T-06).
   Exit: per-language render + hash + provenance.
5. **NATIVE QA** — A native speaker watches one full render per language
   family. Exit: PASS or fix-list (re-translate, re-render affected scenes).
6. **SHIP** — All language renders registered as derived copies of the
   master; a master edit later re-triggers this workflow (T-09).

**Guarded failure modes:** low-resource language quality drop → flagged at
QA, never auto-shipped; glossary conflict between languages → glossary
owner resolves before re-render; master edited mid-run → abort the run,
re-lock the master, restart from stage 2.

workflows.title: Template/API Batch Production (one design, many variants)
workflows.body:
For personalized or series output at scale.

1. **DEFINE TEMPLATE** — Lock the scene manifest template: layout, avatar,
   brand kit, and script with named variables (P-05). A template id is
   minted. Entry: one approved example render. Exit: template passes a
   fallback-reading test (every fallback sounds natural spoken aloud).
2. **SET VARIABLES** — The data table: one row per output, columns for
   every variable. Entry: template id. Exit: table validated — no empty
   cells without declared fallbacks, no variable names starting with a
   number.
3. **BATCH SUBMIT** — Submit jobs asynchronously through the declarative
   API (T-08), with per-job credit estimates from the shared pool (T-11).
   Exit: all jobs accepted; any rejected submission is reported with its
   reason, never silently dropped.
4. **POLL** — Status poller tracks every job; completed renders are
   hashed and stored with their variable row. Exit: N submitted = N
   accounted (rendered or failed-with-reason) — arithmetic reconciliation.
5. **DISTRIBUTE** — Deliver per-row: link/embed/package. Analytics attach
   to the template id for aggregate comparison.
   Exit: distribution list with per-output delivery proof.

**Guarded failure modes:** budget overrun mid-batch → pause at the next
job boundary, report spend, resume only on approval; variable substitution
breaks pronunciation → the row is re-rendered from the correction queue,
not shipped as-is; template changed mid-batch → in-flight jobs finish on
the old template, new jobs take the new one, versions never mixed.

workflows.title: Living Video Maintenance (the program, not the file)
workflows.body:
The workflow that keeps a video library current after publishing.

1. **EDIT** — A detail changes: edit the master text/manifest.
   Entry: change request with the exact new wording.
   Exit: master amended with a change-log entry.
2. **RE-RENDER** — Affected scenes re-render; dependents (translations,
   dubs, variants) re-triggered per T-09.
   Exit: new master hash + per-dependent render status.
3. **AUTO-PROPAGATE** — Shared links, embeds, and LMS packages update to
   the new version automatically.
   Exit: propagation receipt per channel (N channels in = N updated).
4. **ANALYZE** — Built-in analytics: views, completion, per-language and
   per-version comparison.
   Exit: a short read-out: what viewers finished, where they dropped.
5. **ITERATE** — Low-completion segments feed back into a new EDIT cycle.
   Exit: next change request, or "holding — metrics healthy."

**Guarded failure modes:** propagation failure on one channel → the
channel is retried, then escalated; the master version is never rolled
back to hide it; a revoked identity (P-10) triggers re-render or
retirement of affected videos across all channels before the next
propagation cycle.

---

## Cross-workflow rules

- **No orphan renders:** every output references its master id. A render
  without a master is not shippable (composition rule, Master-Script-First).
- **Arithmetic honesty:** batch and localization runs reconcile counts
  (submitted = rendered + failed-with-reason); propagation reconciles
  channels (in = updated). Unreconciled numbers never reach the father.
- **Independent re-review:** any capability the workflow newly depends on
  (a new engine version, a new language pair) passes our merciless review
  (LAW-050) before production use — the ARC-AGI-3 lesson.
- **Voice guardrail:** workflows W-01/W-02/W-03 include voice-synthesis
  stages as GENESIS product capability. The 369 publish path runs the same
  workflows with voice stages disabled — the NO AI VOICE LAW is enforced
  at the gate, not by trust.

workflows.title: TTS Production Pipeline (script → finished audio)
workflows.body:
The pipeline for any non-conversational speech (briefings, announcements,
narrations for the father).

1. **INTAKE** — Text + intent (briefing / announcement) + target voice_id
   + direction note. Entry: voice has a valid P-07 provenance header.
   Exit: intake accepted, or rejected (missing provenance = no render).
2. **NORMALIZE** — P-08 + P-01: strip unpronounceable content, expand
   numbers/acronyms, compute input byte count and cost estimate. Entry:
   intake accepted. Exit: render-ready script + byte cost, or escalation
   if over budget.
3. **DIRECT** — Compile direction (P-02 tags / P-03 director's note) onto
   the normalized script. Entry: render-ready script. Exit: directed
   script with inspectable tag stream.
4. **RENDER** — Generate via the two-stage path (T-01/T-02): semantic plan
   then acoustic render, chunked streaming for long text. Entry: directed
   script. Exit: raw audio.
5. **ROUND-TRIP QC** — Automatic re-transcription (T-11): diff words and
   vocal instructions against the prompt. Check the triple rubric (T-10):
   semantic accuracy, acoustic quality, speaker similarity. Entry: raw
   audio. Exit: PASS → delivery; FAIL → W-02 returns to RENDER (with
   P-06 patch-one-word first), never to delivery.
6. **DELIVER** — Final audio to the requesting module. Entry: QC PASS.
   Exit: delivered with QC report attached (word-error delta, bytes in,
   seconds out, render cost).

Failure modes guarded:
| Failure | Guard |
|---|---|
| Synthetic audio reaches 369 content | Provenance tag checked at delivery; publish gate fails closed on synthetic |
| Mispronunciations / skipped words ship | Round-trip QC fails closed; patch-before-rerender keeps cost down |
| Cost surprise on long renders | Byte count + estimate reported at NORMALIZE, before render |
| Wrong emotion lands on the wrong word | Tag stream is inspectable at DIRECT; QC checks instruction adherence |

techniques.title: Structured Shot Schema (SCENE / IDENTITY / SHOTS / ANATOMY / PHYSICS / CONTINUITY / LIGHTING / AUDIO / LOOK)

Each section has a defined job; the "bad prompt" failure mode is a shot list of angle names with no assigned job per shot.

techniques.genesis_implementation: Make this schema the mandatory brief format for any GENESIS job that produces a multi-shot video (lab builder scripts, the 369 content team's reel briefs). Provide a brief-template file with the nine sections pre-labeled; the pre-generation gate rejects briefs with an empty CONTINUITY section (that's where "the same product must look the same" lives — the section most prompters skip).

workflows.title: Shot Assembly (SceneBuilder discipline)
workflows.body:
For building a sequence from generated clips (lab + report + the 369 video
editor's job).

1. **COLLECT** — Every clip arrives with its provenance: prompt, model, tier,
   ingredients, settings. No clip enters the timeline anonymously.
   Exit: asset register complete.
2. **ORDER** — Drag into narrative order on the timeline; each entry carries
   in/out points and a transition note (cut / match-cut / extend-hop).
   Exit: sequence runs start to finish without gaps.
3. **CONTINUITY CHECK** — Adjacent clips compared for: subject identity,
   lighting direction, camera direction (the 180° rule), audio continuity.
   Exit: all mismatches flagged; Jump-To-style bridges (T-04) planned for
   the gaps.
4. **BRIDGE** — Generate transition hops only where flagged, with
   ingredients re-anchored (T-01) and max-hop discipline (T-11).
   Exit: bridges QC'd individually before joining.
5. **TIMING** — Text overlays and beats timed; export clips individually
   (never rely on the builder's export for final — independent evidence
   shows audio strips on export, so stitch in the real NLE).
   Exit: timeline lock.

Entry: rendered clips + register. Exit: locked timeline, individually
exported clips, stitch note for the NLE.
Failure mode guarded: "export and ship from the builder" — blocked by the
individual-export rule; audio loss is silent otherwise.

workflows.title: Template-Driven Campaign (theme packs at volume)
workflows.body:
- **Entry criteria:** campaign brief (theme, count, platforms); template set
  approved by the format authority; identity tokens registered (or "no
  identity" declared for non-character pieces).
- **Steps:**
  1. Instantiate templates: each slot filled by P-08 (identity + ≤10-word
     scene keywords; text zones reserved, never AI-generated text).
  2. Batch generate (variant batches per slot, W-02 selection per slot).
  3. Series continuity pass: all pieces checked against the campaign manifest
     as a SET, not individually — the family must read as one.
  4. Bulk export at per-platform specs; registry updated with piece ids,
     templates, costs.
- **Exit criteria:** full set delivered at spec; set-level continuity passing;
  per-piece costs reconciled to campaign budget.
- **Guarded failure modes:**
  - One slot keeps failing → swap the template for that slot (templates are
    interchangeable by design) rather than burning credits on a bad fit.
  - Set-level continuity fails → identify the outlier piece(s); regenerate
    the outliers against the manifest, never "accept the set anyway."
  - AI-generated text appears in an image → piece rejected; text is rendered
    by the type system downstream, never by the generator (PERSIAN/typography
    laws apply to all on-piece text).

techniques.title: Emphasis-Calibrated Instruction Design
techniques.what_it_does: On strong instruction-following models, aggressive emphasis (CAPS, MUST, CRITICAL) is dialed back because it causes overtriggering — the model fires the rule where it doesn't apply. Extra guardrails are added only after an observed failure, not by default; safety gates stay unconditional but reason-anchored.

## Capability signals: vendor claims vs. independent evidence

| Capability | Vendor / official signal | Independent evidence |
|---|---|---|
| SWE-bench Verified (code repair) | Opus 4.6: 80.8%; Sonnet 4.6: 79.6% (Anthropic system card) | Compiled reports: Opus 4.7 ~87.6%; GPT-5.5's higher score carries a memorization asterisk per Anthropic's own decontamination analysis — treat leaderboard numbers as harness- and dataset-dependent |
| Terminal-Bench 2.0 (terminal agents) | Sonnet 4.6: 59.1%; Opus 4.6: 65.4% (system card) | Independent comparison: harness choice alone shifts scores 10+ points — the harness is as load-bearing as the model |
| OSWorld (computer use) | Sonnet 4.6: 72.5%; Opus 4.6: 72.7% (system card) | Community comparison: Claude beats GPT-5.3-Codex by ~8.5 pts on GUI navigation tasks — Claude's edge is real on visual/desktop work |
| Long-context retrieval (MRCR v2) | Opus 4.6: 76.0% (system card) | Sonnet 4.6: 51.2% — retrieval strength is tier-dependent, not a family trait; size the model to the retrieval workload |
| Multi-agent research lift | BrowseComp single 74.01% → multi-agent 82.07% (system-card digest) | Practitioner pattern corroborates: parallel researchers + condensed summaries reliably beat single-agent on synthesis tasks |
| Parallel subagent scale | Up to 20 parallel subagents, 3 nesting layers (docs) | Traffic analysis by practitioners: ~92 model calls in 13 min with up to 7 parallel subagents observed on a real fix |
| Pricing | Official price list | Third-party verified Oct 11 2026: Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 (≤100K prompt); prompt-cache reads up to 90% off; batch 50% off; no long-context surcharge on 4.6+ |
| Thinking redaction | Anthropic: redaction hides reasoning from UI only, no reasoning loss | AMD AI head reported performance decline correlated with the redaction rollout — contested by Anthropic, unresolved; lesson: never treat vendor explanation as the final word (our LAW-050) |
| Sycophancy / instruction fade | Anthropic's own research papers document RLHF-driven sycophancy | Practitioners report: standing instructions fade over long sessions; completion bias (claims without proof); task fraud (reporting done without doing) — all independently observed |
| 1M context window | Standard on 4.6+ at standard pricing | Verified in pricing compilations; retrieval quality at 1M is the open question, not the window size |

prompt_patterns.title: Because-Clause Constraints
prompt_patterns.use_when: writing any standing instruction or guardrail.
prompt_patterns.pattern: Never a bare prohibition; always the prohibition plus its reason. Reasons hold gates; bare imperatives cause false triggers.
prompt_patterns.template: > <Rule>, because <what breaks if it is violated and who pays the cost>. > Example shape: "Write tests before claiming a fix, because an untested fix > is a guess and a guess that ships becomes my bug."

- **Use when:** writing any standing instruction or guardrail.
- **Pattern:** Never a bare prohibition; always the prohibition plus its reason.
  Reasons hold gates; bare imperatives cause false triggers.
- **Template:**
  > <Rule>, because <what breaks if it is violated and who pays the cost>.
  > Example shape: "Write tests before claiming a fix, because an untested fix

techniques.title: Co-Editing Workspace (Canvas)
techniques.what_it_does: When the assistant detects a writing or coding task, it opens a split-screen workspace: document/code on one side, chat on the other. Users edit directly or highlight a section and ask for a targeted change; the assistant edits only that section. One-click shortcuts apply common transforms (length, tone, reading level, code review, translate). A version-history slider lets users inspect and restore any prior draft; export goes to PDF/docx/md.
techniques.why_it_works: Chat regenerates everything; co-editing changes one thing. Targeted edits preserve intent and reduce token waste; version history makes experimentation safe (the #1 blocker to asking for bold changes); shortcuts turn repeated prompt patterns into buttons.
techniques.genesis_implementation: The report module should produce artifacts as versioned documents (each edit = new version, restorable), with a "targeted edit" API: `edit_section(doc, range, instruction)` instead of regenerate-all. Offer shortcut transforms for our domain (brand-style polish, Persian↔English tone shifts, format checks). Version history is mandatory — no destructive single-state documents in GENESIS.

prompt_patterns.title: Retry-and-Branch Refinement
prompt_patterns.use_when: an output is close but not right (Canvas-era pattern).
